notes: The VM3200 is a modular 32x32 matrix chassis with 8 input-board slots and 8 output-board slots (4 ports per board); it ships with NO video I/O boards installed, so it has no fixed video connectors of its own. Actual video port count/type/grade depends entirely on which ATEN I/O boards are purchased separately (e.g. VM7804/VM8804 HDMI 4-port boards, VM7814/VM8814 4K HDMI, VM7824/VM8824 true 4K HDMI, VM7904 DisplayPort input, VM7604/VM8604 DVI, VM7104 VGA input, VM7404 3G-SDI input, VM7514/VM8514 HDBaseT, VM7584/VM8584 10G optical/SFP+). Only the fixed chassis ports (power, RS-232, RS-485/422, Ethernet) are listed here as ports; no grade is assigned since these are not bandwidth-graded connector types. Power connector is described by ATEN as a "3-prong socket" on a hot-swappable power module (100-240VAC, 50-60Hz, 10A, ~800W typical); modeled here as IEC (C13/C14 family) which is the standard for this description, though ATEN's own wording does not explicitly say "IEC". A second redundant power module slot exists but is optional/covered and not populated by default, so it is omitted. RS-485/RS-422 port is a 5-pole captcaptive screw / terminal-block connector, modeled as euroblock (closest match; connector list has no generic "terminal block/phoenix connector" id). Confidence is medium because grades are not applicable/confirmable for the fixed ports and the bulk of the device's real I/O is board-dependent and not enumerable as a fixed spec.
